findings.body:
chunk 1/3:

Two provider accounts sharing an app, agent, chat JID and thread match the same consumption query. Intake stores the raw `msg.chat_jid` as `conversationId` and distinguishes accounts in `queueJid` instead (`canonical-message-repository.postgres.ts:369–375`; `shared/thread-queue-key.ts:21–34`). Consequently, `takeInput` can return both accounts' messages, and `consumeAll` can mark another account's pending messages consumed. Preserve provider-account identity in the port and both queries, and add an integration test with otherwise identical routes on two accounts.
findings.title: Include provider-account identity in the consumption scope

findings.body:
chunk 1/3:

The crossing and concurrent-consumer tests exercise repositories directly. They do not prove delivery of late input, release after failure before a reply, retention after failure following a reply, or consumption across settings reload and restart through the real entry point. Existing lifecycle coverage does not supply that proof: `apps/core/test/e2e/claim-protocol-two-process.postgres.e2e.test.ts:638–643` checks the old cursor, while `apps/core/test/agent-e2e/scenarios/boot-restart.agent-e2e.test.ts:114–143` checks agent configuration survival. Add the required lifecycle scenarios with delivery-count and persisted-consumption assertions. The review contract explicitly keeps missing tests at P1.
findings.title: Not done: no-loss/no-duplication end-to-end tests

findings.body:
chunk 1/3:

These storage operations have no production callers, as intended for T1. Runtime admission still uses `getOrRecoverCursor` and `collectPendingMessagesSince` (`apps/core/src/runtime/message-loop.ts:497–509`), and group processing still reads through the cursor (`apps/core/src/runtime/group-processing.ts:96–108`). Done-when item 2 therefore remains dependent on T2's coordinated reader/writer and recovery switch and T4's runner delivery confirmations. Track this functional gap with those tasks; the repository addition alone does not deliver the story's guarantee.
findings.title: Later: T2 and T4 must complete message delivery and failure recovery

findings.body:
chunk 1/3:

The branch adds `plans/TURN-1.md`, `plans/TURN-1.read.md` and `.factory/stories/TURN-1/**`, including the seven-task plan and historical review findings. These paths are outside the permitted scope and are not needed to implement or test the storage contract. Move those artifacts to a separately scoped change. The repository port and Postgres integration-test changes are necessary for this task.
findings.title: Remove story-wide planning and review artifacts from the scoped change

findings.body:
chunk 3/3:

The new crossing test calls repository methods directly; it never starts a turn, delivers a reply, reloads settings, or restarts a worker. It therefore cannot prove the required end-to-end guarantees for late messages and failures before versus after replying. The existing two-process test at apps/core/test/e2e/claim-protocol-two-process.postgres.e2e.test.ts:424 covers one inbound message, without these consumption scenarios. Add the required real-entry-point tests asserting delivery counts and remaining unconsumed items across two workers, settings reload, restart, and both failure boundaries. Although production wiring belongs to T2/T4, the review contract explicitly keeps missing test coverage at P1.
findings.title: Not done: No message is lost or given twice.

findings.body:
chunk 3/3:

The branch adds plans/TURN-1.md and plans/TURN-1.read.md, although the permitted documentation scope is docs/decisions/0103-*. These files contain the seven-task story plan and a prior review receipt; neither is needed to implement or test T1's persistence contract. Move both additions to a separate planning change. The repository port and integration-test changes are necessary for this task and do not have the same scope issue.
findings.title: Remove the story-wide planning artifacts from this scoped change
